summary: Well-executed preregistered paired study with artifact-backed traceability that tests sanitizer + verifier gating in an LLM-driven NetOps pipeline. Confirmatory analysis is reproducible from archived artifacts and shows a small, statistically detectable paired increase in validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline; authors correctly disclose a protocol deviation (unset temperature) and the unexecuted benign-control. The manuscript is scientifically useful but requires a few concrete, manuscript-level fixes before finalisation.
critical_issues: Disclosure Statement in the submitted manuscript is overly verbose and duplicates execution-level artifact paths/hashes and run-internal logs that should be kept in the archived evidence bundle rather than repeated in manuscript prose. Condense the Disclosure so it is concise and science-focused while preserving the mandatory content (models, orchestration, autonomy boundary, protocol deviation).

Some bibliographic items and artifact references appear as raw DOIs/URLs or run-internal paths in manuscript prose. Per track requirements, replace prose DOI/URL/path insertions with standard IEEE numbered citations in the body and move run-internal paths/hashes to the archived manifest; do not present file-level provenance as ordinary narrative.

A planned preregistered item (benign-control and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand) was not executed. Although the manuscript discloses this omission, ensure that the Methods and Results sections prominently state (a) that the benign-control was not executed, (b) which confirmatory/secondary inferences are therefore uncomputed, and (c) the consequence for interpretation of the primary estimand (i.e., no empirical false-positive-blocking rate is available).
required_revisions: Condense the Disclosure Statement within the five-page manuscript: keep mandatory content (models used, orchestration, autonomy-lock boundary, protocol deviations, high-level artifact availability) but remove per-file paths and full hashes from the main text; instead cite the archived execution manifest and provide the full hash manifest in the artifact archive referenced from the Disclosure.

Convert any DOI/URL/run-path occurrences in narrative prose to standard IEEE numbered citations and ensure each cited reference actually supports the immediately adjacent scholarly claim (fix any inline DOI/URL citations to numeric form).

Prominently and unambiguously state in Methods and Results that the preregistered benign-control (M=50) and associated false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed, and explictly limit claims that would have required those results. This disclosure must appear in Methods and Results (not only in Conclusion or Disclosure).
optional_revisions: Add a short, explicit paragraph summarizing practical significance given ceiling effects (guarded = 100%) and small discordant count (n10=6), to help readers interpret operational relevance beyond statistical detectability.

Include a brief table or appendix (archived artifact) enumerating the six discordant pairs with high-level diagnostic labels (sanitizer-only vs repair-applied) to clarify repair vs sanitization contributions; keep any low-level traces in the archived bundle, not in the main manuscript.

State clearly the recommended exact provider sampling setting for deterministic reproduction (e.g., temperature=0) and point readers to the artifact path that contains the full machine-readable execution manifest so reproducibility steps are unambiguous.
